findings.name: Open
findings.description: Source and Cross-Platform**: All codes and model weights are publicly available for research purposes. CodeGeeX supports both Ascend and NVIDIA platforms. It supports inference in a single Ascend 910,
5-16**: CodeGeeX paper has been accepted by [KDD 2023, Long Beach](https://kdd.org/kdd2023/) and will be represented during the conference.
03-30**: CodeGeeX paper is now available at [arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17568).
02-14**: CodeGeeX now supports [Cloud Studio](https://cloudstudio.net/), a fantastic web IDE from Tencent. Click on the badge on top of this page to quickly launch an environment to test CodeGeeX.

02-13**: Thanks a lot to [OneFlow](https://github.com/Oneflow-Inc/oneflow) team for adding oneflow backend for CodeGeeX's inference (Even faster than FasterTransformer under FP16!). Check more details
02**: We are hosting [CodeGeeX "Coding With AI" Hackathon](https://dorahacks.io/hackathon/codegeex/), design cool applications based on CodeGeeX and win prizes (RTX 4090, DJI drone, etc)!
12-31**: We release the FasterTransformer version of CodeGeeX in [codegeex-fastertransformer](https://github.com/CodeGeeX/codegeex-fastertransformer). The INT8 accelerated version reaches an a verage

12-13**: We release the source code of CodeGeeX VS Code extension in [codegeex-vscode-extension](https://github.com/CodeGeeX/codegeex-vscode-extension). Follow [QuickStart](https://github.com/CodeGeeX
12-11**: CodeGeeX is now available for Jetbrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, CLion, etc), download it [here](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/20587-codegeex).
12-04**: We release source code of quantization (requires less GPU RAM: 27GB -> 15GB) and model parallelism (possible to run on multiple GPUs with <8G RAM).
09-30**: We release the cross-platform source code and models weights for both Ascend and NVIDIA platforms.
